why: Karma answers Bard by refusing his roam timing: Mantra-empowered Inner Flame and shields match Bard's lane poke, and Focused Resolve threatens the root if Bard steps up for Cosmic Binding. When Bard leaves for chimes or a Magical Journey play, Karma shoves the wave and punishes the stranded bot laner, and in fights her Mantra shield and speed keep carries from being isolated by Tempered Fate. That held across 31 pro games at a 67.7% win rate for Karma.
tips: Shove the wave hard whenever Bard leaves lane so his roam costs plates or farm.
Save Mantra for the shield and speed boost when a fight starts, not for extra poke.
Hold Focused Resolve until Bard has used his portal or is locked in place by a teammate.

why: Lulu answers Milio by winning the short, targeted trade he wants to stretch out: Help, Pix! shields through his poke, Glitterlance slows his follow-up, and Whimsy polymorphs his carry mid-all-in so Cozy Campfire's extra range goes unused. Wild Growth then out-values Breath of Life in a committed 2v2 because it adds health and a knock-up while Milio's cleanse has nothing to remove. Lulu took 60.9% of 23 pro games in this pairing.
tips: Polymorph the enemy carry the moment an all-in starts, not the support.
Shield your carry before trading so Pix attacks add damage on every auto.
Save Wild Growth for the committed dive or all-in instead of topping off health in lane.

why: Seraphine answers Karma by out-ranging the poke war and scaling the fight: Stage Presence roots or charms Karma when she steps up for Mantra poke, and Surround Sound shields and hastes her carry through Karma's burst window. Once the first poke exchange ends, Seraphine's waveclear keeps Karma from crashing waves for free, and Encore turns Karma's forward posture into a teamfight catch.
tips: Root Karma when she steps forward to cast, then walk away before her return poke lands.
Use your shield and speed boost to disengage after short trades instead of extending them.
Hold your ultimate for grouped targets in river or lane chokes rather than firing it at one poking enemy.

why: Seraphine answers Milio by forcing the long fight his heals want to avoid ending quickly: her root and Encore charm lock a target in place longer than one Breath of Life cleanse can cover, and Surround Sound matches Cozy Campfire's sustain for her own carry. Because Milio has no hard engage, Seraphine freely stacks passive notes behind the wave and wins grouped river fights where her ultimate hits multiple targets.
tips: Build up your empowered cast behind the wave and spend it on a root, not on farm.
Wait for Milio's cleanse ultimate before committing your charm ultimate to a fight.
Shield and speed your whole group when rotating to objectives so you arrive set up first.

why: Rakan answers Milio with engage speed Milio cannot kite: Grand Entrance arrives before Cozy Campfire value builds, and The Quickness chains a charm after the knock-up so Breath of Life cleanses only part of the chain. Milio's kickback is single-target and telegraphed, while Rakan re-engages with Battle Dance mobility once it is spent. The pairing went 72.2% for Rakan across 18 pro games, and the current one-liner in the app makes the same point: the knock-up lands before Milio can kick him away.
tips: Engage with your ultimate already active so the charm follows the knock-up without a gap.
Dash to an ally to reset, then re-enter once Milio's kickback and cleanse are spent.
Start fights from fog or a flank instead of running straight through his carry's extra range.

why: Shen answers Alistar by making the all-in target the wrong target: Stand United shields whoever Alistar combos, Shadow Dash taunts Alistar off his carry mid-combo, and Spirit's Refuge blocks the auto-attacks that follow the knock-up. Alistar also telegraphs his engage by walking or flashing in, which gives Shen time to arrive from a roam. The pro edge is narrow at 56.3% over 16 games, and solo-queue data cuts the other way, so this is a coordination pick rather than a lane stomp.
tips: Keep your ultimate ready for the enemy all-in target instead of using it to join your own engage.
Taunt the diver off your carry first, then use your sword block zone to cover the retreat.
Roam only when your ultimate is up so you can still answer a bot-lane all-in.

why: Nautilus answers Alistar by out-ranging the engage and winning the counter-punch: Dredge Line and Depth Charge lock Alistar down from farther than Pulverize reaches, and Riptide plus his passive root stop Alistar walking at the carry. If Alistar combos first, Nautilus hooks or ults the enemy carry in return, and his shield lets him survive being the focus. Nautilus won 66.7% of 15 pro games in this pairing.
tips: Hook the enemy carry when Alistar commits, rather than peeling with the hook.
Use your point-and-click ultimate on the carry who follows Alistar in, not on Alistar himself.
Stand in hook range of your carry so Alistar must cross you to reach them.

why: Nautilus answers Milio in pro play by chaining more crowd control than one cleanse removes: Depth Charge into Dredge Line into a passive root sequences Milio's Breath of Life early, and the second and third locks still land. His hook also threatens from outside Cozy Campfire range, forcing Milio to play back and give up lane pressure. This only works with instant team follow-up, because Milio cleanses a lone hook for free; Nautilus still took 66.7% of 15 pro games.
tips: Open with your ultimate and follow with hook so the cleanse cannot erase the whole chain.
Only hook when a teammate is in range to damage the target during the lock.
After Milio cleanses once, stay in position and threaten a second engage before his ultimate returns.

why: Shen answers support Camille by denying the isolation she plays for: Stand United shields the target of Hextech Ultimatum and arrives inside the cage with her, Shadow Dash can taunt her off the carry, and Spirit's Refuge blocks her empowered auto-attacks. Camille also needs wall angles to engage, while Shen's value travels with his team wherever she jumps. Shen won 60.0% of 15 pro games here.
tips: Ultimate the ally Camille locks down so she never gets a clean one-versus-one inside her cage.
Taunt Camille the moment she lands rather than chasing her support partner.
Keep your block zone for her empowered attack sequence after she dashes in.

why: Renata Glasc answers Lulu by punishing the clump Lulu wants: Handshake roots through the wave, Hostile Takeover turns Lulu's own carry and polymorph timing against her team, and Bailout revives the target Lulu's team bursts through Wild Growth. Lulu must stand near her carry to shield and grow them, which keeps both in Renata's ultimate cone. Renata took 64.3% of 14 pro games.
tips: Fire your ultimate when Lulu groups around her carry to shield them, not at scattered targets.
Use Bailout on the ally being bursted first; the revival and attack speed swing the trade.
Root through the minion wave when Lulu steps up to shield, since she must come into range.

why: Leona answers Nautilus by being the tankier, faster starter in the hook lane: Solar Flare out-ranges Dredge Line, Zenith Blade goes through the wave he hides behind, and Eclipse lets her survive the hook she baits out. When Nautilus hooks her instead of her carry, she turns on his carry with a full stun chain while his anchor is down. Leona won 76.9% of 13 pro games in this pairing.
tips: Let Nautilus hook you, then immediately engage his carry while his anchor is on cooldown.
Open grouped fights with your ultimate from range instead of walking in for a blade engage.
Activate your damage-reduction ability before the hook lands so the trade starts in your favour.

why: Lulu answers Karma by nullifying the poke-and-burst pattern: Help, Pix! shields Mantra poke on reaction, Whimsy polymorphs Karma or her carry when Focused Resolve starts channeling, and Wild Growth out-scales Karma's shield in the 2v2 all-in. Karma also has no hard engage to stop Lulu's carry walking forward behind Pix damage. Lulu took 69.2% of 13 pro games.
tips: Shield the ally Karma is focusing the moment her empowered cast animation starts.
Polymorph the tethered target's attacker or Karma herself to break her root setup.
Use your speed boost to chase after winning a shield trade, not to start trades.

why: Shen answers Bard by matching the roam without leaving lane defenceless: Stand United follows Bard's Magical Journey plays anywhere on the map, and his taunt plus sword block win the 2v2 when Bard returns through a portal. Bard's Tempered Fate also gives Shen a free arrival window, since a frozen ally can be shielded and joined as the stasis ends. Shen won 69.2% of 13 pro games.
tips: Match Bard's roams with your ultimate instead of walking the same path late.
Time your arrival to land as a frozen ally's stasis ends so you can taunt immediately.
Taunt through Bard's portal exit when he brings teammates into your lane.

why: Nautilus answers Rell by interrupting and out-lasting her one engage: a passive root or Dredge Line stops Crash Down's follow-up, Depth Charge locks Rell or her carry before Magnet Storm pulls the team in, and his shield wins the extended tank trade while Rell is dismounted and slow. If Rell misses or is stopped, she has no second engage. Nautilus took 66.7% of 12 pro games.
tips: Save your hook or ultimate to stop Rell's follow-up crowd control, not to start every fight.
Focus Rell while she is dismounted and slow after her engage ends.
Hook the carry who steps up to follow Rell's engage rather than trading into her shield.

why: Seraphine answers Lulu by playing outside polymorph range and winning the grouped fight: her root and Encore reach farther than Whimsy, Surround Sound shields her carry through Pix poke, and her waveclear denies Lulu the slow push she wants around a scaling carry. In 5v5s a multi-target charm out-values one Wild Growth. Seraphine won 66.7% of 12 pro games.
tips: Stay at maximum range and spend empowered casts on roots so Lulu never reaches polymorph range.
Save your charm ultimate for when Lulu has already used Wild Growth on her carry.
Shield your group on the way into river fights so you take the first position.

why: Nautilus answers Lulu by removing the reaction window she plays around: Depth Charge is point-and-click, so polymorph cannot stop it, and Dredge Line plus his passive root chain past a single shield or Wild Growth knock-up. Lulu also has no mobility to escape a hook lane once flash is down. Nautilus won 66.7% of 12 pro games, provided the hook or ultimate is followed instantly before Whimsy resets the fight.
tips: Open with your point-and-click ultimate when Lulu is in range instead of fishing with hooks.
Chain hook and your passive root on the same target so one shield cannot save them.
After Lulu uses polymorph defensively, stay forward and threaten again before it returns.

why: Shen answers Nautilus by turning the hook into his engage: being pulled in puts Shadow Dash in range of Nautilus's carry, Spirit's Refuge blocks the follow-up autos, and Stand United shields whichever ally Depth Charge targets. Nautilus's lockdown is single-target and sequential, so Shen's arrival makes it a numbers fight. Shen took 66.7% of 12 pro games, though the sample is older.
tips: Accept a hook onto yourself and taunt forward onto the enemy carry as you land.
Ultimate the ally targeted by the point-and-click knock-up so the engage lands on a shielded target.
Block with your sword zone while retreating after the first crowd-control chain ends.

why: Shen answers Rell by arriving after her engage commits: Stand United shields the Crash Down target and teleports Shen into the Magnet Storm, where Shadow Dash taunts Rell and her follow-up off the carry. Rell's engage is also her only mobility, so once it is spent Shen's block zone and taunt win the long trade. Shen won 58.3% of 12 pro games.
tips: Wait for Rell to commit her engage before ulting in, so she cannot redirect onto you.
Taunt the attackers following Rell rather than Rell herself if your carry is still in danger.
Use your block zone while dismounted Rell is being focused to deny her team's autos.

why: Lulu answers Bard by making his picks too expensive: Whimsy polymorphs whoever Bard portals onto, Help, Pix! plus Wild Growth out-shield a Cosmic Binding burst, and Glitterlance slows his roam return through chokepoints. Bard must leave lane to scale with chimes, and Lulu shoves and pokes the abandoned carry in that window. Lulu won 72.7% of 11 pro games.
tips: Polymorph the first enemy who comes through Bard's portal, before they cast.
Shove and poke hard whenever Bard leaves to collect chimes or roam.
Save Wild Growth for the target Bard freezes or binds, not for lane sustain.

why: Karma answers Milio by out-poking the sustain lane and out-running its disengage: Mantra Inner Flame pokes from outside Cozy Campfire value range, her shield and speed let her carry dodge the kickback, and Focused Resolve threatens Milio himself when he steps up to heal. Milio heals poke in long lanes, so Karma forces short, repeated bursts and roams first with lane priority. Karma won 77.8% of 9 pro games.
tips: Spend Mantra on poke before fights so Milio enters every skirmish already healing from behind.
Root Milio when he steps forward, since he has no dash to break the tether.
Use your shield speed to leave lane first after crashing a wave.

why: Nautilus answers Karma by ending the poke lane with one hook: Karma has no dash, so Dredge Line plus his passive root holds her for a full trade, and Depth Charge guarantees the engage when she shields and speeds away. Her Mantra shield absorbs poke, not a chained all-in with follow-up. The pro margin is thin at 55.6% over 9 games, so this works only when the hook is paired with instant damage.
tips: Hook Karma herself rather than her carry, since she has no dash to escape.
Wait for her shield speed boost to fade before committing your ultimate.
Stay in brush to shorten her poke range advantage before you engage.

why: Seraphine answers Nautilus by never letting him walk into hook range for free: her root stops his approach, Surround Sound shields and speeds her carry out of Depth Charge follow-up, and Encore reverses a hook engage into a multi-target charm. Nautilus also has no sustain, so repeated poke between engages leaves him too low to start. Seraphine won 75.0% of 8 pro games.
tips: Root Nautilus as he walks forward to hook instead of saving the root for his carry.
Shield and speed your carry sideways out of hook angles, not straight backwards.
Counter-engage with your ultimate only after Nautilus has committed forward.

why: Renata Glasc answers Seraphine by punishing her grouped, forward-facing setup: Hostile Takeover hits the clump Seraphine shields inside, Handshake roots through the wave she hides behind, and Bailout saves the target of an Encore charm engage. Seraphine also casts in place for her ultimate, giving Renata a clean window to fire back. Renata took 75.0% of 8 pro games.
tips: Fire your ultimate into the group Seraphine is shielding, not at her backline alone.
Save Bailout for the ally caught by her charm so they revive into the counter-fight.
Root through minions when she steps up to clear the wave.

why: Rakan answers Renata Glasc by engaging faster than Hostile Takeover can be aimed: The Quickness plus Grand Entrance chains charm into knock-up before her carry can be bailed out, and Battle Dance repositions him out of Handshake range. Renata wants a slow front-to-back fight; Rakan makes it a dive she must answer instantly. Rakan won 75.0% of 8 pro games, matching the app's existing Renata answer logic of starting before the disengage lands.
tips: Start with your ultimate active and dash in from an angle her root cannot cover.
Burst the target before Bailout's revival window can be triggered by a kill.
Dash back to an ally after the first chain, then re-engage when her ultimate is down.

why: Camille answers Rell by isolating her from the follow-up she needs: Hextech Ultimatum cages Rell or her carry alone, Hookshot mobility dodges or exits Crash Down's area, and her shield plus true damage wins the extended duel while Rell is dismounted. Rell's engage also clusters her team for a cage on the carry behind her. Camille won 85.7% of just 7 pro games, so treat the rate as directional.
tips: Cage Rell's carry away from her instead of duelling Rell inside her pull.
Use your wall dash to leave her engage area, then re-enter on your own timing.
Wait for her dismount before committing your ultimate, when she cannot escape it.

why: Bard answers Nautilus by refusing the hook lane entirely: Caretaker's Shrines and chime speed let him leave before Nautilus sets up, Magical Journey pulls his carry out of hook angles, and Tempered Fate freezes Nautilus's engage or the follow-up behind it. When Nautilus does hook, a point-blank Cosmic Binding against terrain answers in place. Bard won 71.4% of 7 pro games.
tips: Leave lane on chime routes before Nautilus can set up a hook from brush.
Freeze Nautilus or his follow-up with your ultimate when a hook does land.
Bind Nautilus against nearby terrain when he walks at you, then portal away.

why: Leona answers support Camille by locking her before the cage matters: Zenith Blade and Shield of Daybreak chain stuns through Camille's dash, Solar Flare out-ranges her wall engage, and Eclipse lets Leona body-block Hextech Ultimatum's target. Camille needs a clean isolated duel; Leona turns it into a grouped stun chain. The margin is modest at 57.1% over 7 games.
tips: Hold your stun for after Camille dashes in instead of opening with it from range.
Stand on your carry so Camille must cross your blade to reach them.
Open with your ultimate when she takes a wall position to engage.

why: Leona answers Alistar by starting first and surviving his combo better: Solar Flare initiates from beyond Pulverize range, Zenith Blade roots through his engage, and Eclipse plus her stun chain let her turn onto his carry while his combo is spent. Alistar pushing her away also fails to stop a blade already in flight. Leona won all 6 pro games sampled, a perfect but very small sample.
tips: Initiate from ultimate range before Alistar can walk or flash into combo range.
If he combos your carry, engage his carry immediately instead of chasing him.
Trigger your damage reduction before his knock-up lands to win the tank trade.

why: Seraphine answers Shen by keeping him at root range and winning after his arrival: her empowered root stops Shadow Dash follow-through, Surround Sound shields the Stand United target's opposite number, and Encore charms Shen and whoever he ulted as they group. Shen also has no poke answer, so he enters fights already softened. Seraphine won 83.3% of 6 pro games.
tips: Root Shen the moment he taunts forward so his team cannot follow through.
Charm the grouped targets after Shen arrives on an ally, not before he commits.
Poke Shen down between fights since he has no way to heal it off in lane.

why: Lux answers Bard by out-ranging his setup and deleting his return path: Light Binding roots Bard or his portal exit, Lucent Singularity zones the chokepoints he roams through, and her shield covers Cosmic Binding burst. Bard must walk forward to bind or place shrines, which is exactly where Lux's full combo waits. Lux won 83.3% of 6 pro games.
tips: Aim your root at Bard's portal exit when he returns to lane with teammates.
Zone the river entrances Bard roams through instead of throwing spells at the wave.
Shield your carry before Bard's binding connects so the burst trade is already lost for him.

why: Seraphine answers Bard by shoving him in and out-scaling his roam: her waveclear pins Bard to lane, her root punishes his portal returns, and Surround Sound plus Encore win the grouped fights his Tempered Fate tries to start. If Bard leaves anyway, Seraphine takes plates and arrives to fights with a multi-target charm he cannot match. Seraphine won 83.3% of 6 pro games.
tips: Clear waves quickly to keep Bard in lane and deny his roam windows.
Hold your charm ultimate for the fight Bard starts with his freeze, after targets unfreeze grouped.
Shield your group while rotating so Bard cannot pick a straggler on the way.

why: Renata Glasc answers Alistar by turning his engage into her fight: Hostile Takeover fired into his combo makes his own team attack each other, Handshake roots him mid-approach, and Bailout revives the carry he combos. Alistar must come to melee range to do anything, which guarantees her ultimate cone connects. Renata won 66.7% of 6 pro games.
tips: Hold your ultimate until Alistar commits forward, then fire it through his whole team.
Bailout the ally Alistar combos at the start of the fight, not after they fall.
Root Alistar as he walks in so his combo starts from too far away.

why: Seraphine answers Alistar by stopping the walk-in and reversing the dive: her root holds him outside Pulverize range, Surround Sound speeds her carry out of combo reach, and Encore charms Alistar plus his follow-up after he commits. He also has no poke, so repeated lane poke leaves him too low to all-in. Seraphine won 66.7% of 6 pro games.
tips: Root Alistar during his approach rather than saving it for after he engages.
Speed your carry diagonally away when he flashes in, not in a straight line.
Save your charm ultimate for his follow-up attackers, not Alistar alone.

why: Bard answers Milio by leaving the sustain lane and deciding fights elsewhere: Magical Journey roams arrive before Milio can follow, Tempered Fate freezes his carry or his cleanse timing, and Cosmic Binding threatens the wall-adjacent fights Milio's extra range wants. Milio answers one engage, not a portal flank plus a freeze. Bard won 66.7% of 6 pro games.
tips: Roam through your portal while Milio is pinned healing his carry in lane.
Freeze Milio's carry to force his cleanse early, then engage again before it returns.
Fight near walls so your binding can stun when Milio steps up to heal.

why: Alistar answers Rell by breaking her one engage sequence: Headbutt knocks her out of Crash Down follow-up or away from his carry, Pulverize interrupts Magnet Storm's pull, and Unbreakable Will lets him stand inside her combo and keep peeling. Once Rell is dismounted and displaced, she cannot re-engage. Alistar won 66.7% of 6 pro games.
tips: Headbutt Rell away the instant she lands instead of knocking up her whole team.
Save your knock-up to interrupt her pull when she gathers your teammates.
Use your ultimate to stay in front of your carry while Rell is dismounted and slow.
